A contract is not considered to be a derivative where ils purpose is to take physical delivery in the normal course
of business, unless the entity has a practice of settling the contracts on a net basis.
In the case of Selteo, while the company often takes physical delivery of the edible oil, it does so only to sell shortly
afterwards, and usually settles on a net basis. Thus the contracts will be considered to be derivative contracts
rather than contracts for purchase of inventory. Derivatives are accounted for at fair value through profit or loss,
